findings.issue: A-3's { durability: 'strict' } is not checked by any every-push test. Removing it leaves all Vitest and every-push e2e tests green. The opt-in SIGKILL test is unlikely to catch it either, because killing the process does not drop the OS page cache (relaxed durability only loses data on an OS or power crash).
findings.evidence: No test in tests/storage/* or e2e/hand-records.spec.ts checks the transaction options. fake-indexeddb ignores durability.
findings.fix: In tests/storage/hand-store.test.ts, wrap the fake IDBFactory's IDBDatabase.prototype.transaction (or pass a factory whose open result is proxied) to record the third argument, and assert that add() passes { durability: 'strict' }.

findings.issue: This happens only when a write is slow. The user clicks Deal next during the review, which sets holdNextHand to false and starts a 1.5 s timer. If the write is still pending when that timer fires, both continuations are chained on write.current and both call newCode(). The first deals and the second updater is a no-op, so one code is drawn and thrown away. In the normal fast path the deal changes `table` before the timer fires, and cleanup cancels the timer, so there is exactly one draw, the same as before this change. Codes are independent CSPRNG draws, so the user's hand and replay are unaffected; the only effect would be on e2e draw counters in the slow path.
findings.evidence: Table.onDealNext calls setReview(null) and then dealNext(). The effect re-runs with holdNextHand false (line 136) and arms the timer (line 139). Both .then callbacks (lines 140 and 164) run back to back in microtasks with no render between them, so `cancelled` is still false.
findings.fix: Optional: keep a shared `dealing` ref that the first continuation sets and the second checks before calling newCode(). Or leave it as is and note it in docs/storage/hand-records.md.

summary: All 20 SPEC items are implemented as specified and each named test would fail on a broken implementation. Checks done: the delayed-write e2e asserts Hand #1 and 0 records at T+1900 and saved:1 before header:2; the churn e2e would never deal if the timer restarted; the fail store checks the console, pageerror and unhandledrejection; ConstraintError leaves the record unchanged and the store has no put, update or delete; the parser fault table names each field. Race review: (1) Unmount or Leave during a pending write: the auto-deal continuation checks `cancelled`. The dealNext continuation has no guard, but setTable after unmount is a no-op and the write itself completes. (2) StrictMode: the harness runs under StrictMode. The `reported` ref survives the simulated remount, so there is no double write. The useState(newSessionId) initializer may run twice, but only one id is kept, so there is one id per mount. (3) The onHandComplete ref is updated in a dependency-free effect and removed from the main effect's dependencies; handStore and sessionId are stable. (4) Deal-next plus timer: a discarded second code is drawn only in the slow-write path. The fast-path draw sequence is unchanged, so this is a NIT, not MAJOR. (5) Record fields match AC#4, including bot ids for replacements (SPEC-08, SPEC-17). (6) The test seams live only in e2e/support. Nothing under src/ imports them, and grep finds no setTimeout in src/storage or hand-record.ts. I ran e2e/hand-records.spec.ts and next-hand.spec.ts on Chromium and WebKit: 24 tests passed in 6.8 s, so the every-push cost is small. The tests wait on real IndexedDB through auto-waiting assertions or expect.poll, and the fake-time assertions are bounded by the paused clock, so flake risk is low. Unit tests passed (16 tests). The only gap: strict durability has no test (MINOR). There are no BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
